title: You keep asking God for order…
paragraphs:
You keep asking God for order…
but you resist His authority.
Because this is where most people get it wrong.

You love the idea of “divine alignment.”
You post about “God’s timing.”
You pray for breakthrough.
You want the blessing… without the government.
And that tension is exposing something.
🔥 Here’s the open loop you can’t ignore:
Why does God repeat the number 12… again… and again… and again?
Why 12—when He builds His people, His leadership, even heaven itself?
We don’t struggle with believing in God.
We struggle with submitting to Him.

We want a Savior…
but not a King.

We want comfort…
but not correction.

We want grace…
but not governance.

You can go to church
and still resist God’s authority.

You can quote Scripture
and still live self-ruled.

You can say “Lord, Lord”…
and still sit on the throne of your own life.
📖 SCRIPTURE ANCHOR — God Reveals His Pattern
Throughout Scripture, God establishes 12 as a number of divine government.
1. 12 Tribes of Israel — Structure of God’s People
“All these are the twelve tribes of Israel…” — Genesis 49:28
God didn’t build a scattered crowd.
“He called his twelve disciples to him and gave them authority…” — Matthew 10:1
He was reestablishing God’s government—this time through grace.
“It had a great, high wall with twelve gates… The wall of the city had twelve foundations…” — Revelation 21:12–14
“For to us a child is born… and the government shall be upon His shoulder…” — Isaiah 9:6
Some scholars interpret the number 12 symbolically—as completeness in leadership or divine administration.
Others see it as a consistent pattern of God organizing His people under authority.
But across interpretations, one truth stands:

God is a God of order, not chaos.
(1 Corinthians 14:33)
And God does not negotiate His throne.
✝️ GOSPEL TURN — Where Grace Breaks In
This is where it gets real.
Because if God is truly King…
Then we are all guilty of rebellion.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
Every one of us has stepped out from under His authority.
But here’s the shock of grace:
Jesus Christ stepped into our chaos.
Lived in perfect submission to the Father.
“Not my will, but Yours be done.” — Luke 22:42
Then He took our rebellion… to the cross.
Every moment we said, “My will over Yours.”
“Christ died for our sins… He was buried… He was raised on the third day.” — 1 Corinthians 15:3–4
is the Savior inviting us back.
But to be restored under His loving rule.
The number 12 is not about math.
And the question is no longer:
Is He Lord over your life?
and still not surrender to Him.
You can know about His government…
and still live in your own.

The control.
The pride.
The hidden sin.
Come under the authority of Christ.

but as a son.
as a daughter.
Because His rule is not harsh.
If you’re ready to surrender fully—not halfway, not selectively—
And if this message opened your eyes…
